scene: A cartoon man with an egg-shaped head and round wide eyes looking up and to his right stands at lower left in a navy T-shirt printed BROKE above a red swoosh-like mark, with a calculator lying on the floor by his foot. To the right a dark monitor-like panel is stacked with grey bars carrying green dollar circles and red dots; a red GYM MEMBERSHIP card and a MONTHLY SUBSCRIPTION label stick out of it, and a small grey car with a red shield icon sits at its base. A thick black curved arrow from the right edge points at the panel; the background is plain white.
mechanism: A named-trap proposition: the headline promises a trap and the right-hand pile of subscription cards and money bubbles drains out of a screen while a shirt labelled BROKE shows the cost.
composition: A full-width headline fills the top third, with the man on the left third and the subscription panel on the right half forming two equal masses. The arrow at far right returns the eye to the panel. White negative space keeps the groups apart, but the panel itself packs about ten small icons.
typography: Four words in one line of heavy black capitals span nearly the whole width and stay fully legible at 160x90. The small label texts on the cards, including the garbled digits on the subscription tag, vanish at phone size. The headline does not name subscriptions, which the title supplies.
colors: Black and white base with navy shirt and blue jeans, then small saturated red and green accents on the cards and dollar bubbles. Red marks the cost-draining items while green belongs to the money circles; the white ground separates every object cleanly.
psychology: The wide round eyes and slightly puckered mouth read as puzzled or startled in cartoon terms. The shirt word BROKE and the calculator on the floor are explicit visible shorthand for money trouble.
partnership: Title says Subscription Trap That's Keeping You Poor; the thumbnail repeats trap and adds gym card, monthly tag and cost-bubble icons that make subscriptions concrete. The unanswered part is which subscriptions matter and how large the leak is.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: black headline first, then the BROKE-shirted man's face, then the red GYM card on the panel, with the arrow nudging back to the panel last.
art: Flat vector cartoon with thick outlines and white background; the panel has a slightly odd perspective and the MONTHLY SUBSCRIPTION tag carries garbled characters (35 -35 /6AD), which is a visible text artefact. The man is clean and holds up at 160x90 even though the panel is busy.
strength: Headline plus a simple BROKE-labelled character gives an instant who-and-what read.
weakness: The panel is crowded with tiny cards and icons whose text is garbled and lost at phone size.
bottleneck: The right half asks the viewer to decode many small objects before the idea of subscriptions lands.
action: Hypothesis: reduce the panel to three large labelled items (gym card, one app tag, one monthly price) and test whether the trap reads faster at 160x90.
counterexample: Seq 7 keeps one large number and one object per side, so its message needs fewer decoding steps than the crowded panel here.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: At the left a grey-shirted cartoon man with spiky black hair and a level mouth sits at a wooden table holding a heap of green cash banded in front of him. Across the table four smiling people stand close together: a woman with a plate of food, an older grey-haired man, a young man holding a red-wrapped gift with a yellow bow, and a girl in red. A red curved arrow from the headline points at the woman, and a window with green trees sits behind the left of the room.
mechanism: A two-sided contrast between the lone cash-holder and a warm crowd bringing food and gifts, so the picture itself shows how a group reacts to wealth.
composition: The man occupies the left third while four faces crowd the right half, with the arrow bridging the headline and the woman. The table runs across the lower frame as a base line. The group faces are close to each other and the gift and plate give secondary points, but the background room adds some clutter.
typography: Four words in white outlined capitals sit across the top, and HOW THEY TREAT YOU stays readable in the 160 render despite the low native resolution of 360x202. The words omit any wealth level, which the title supplies with from $0 to $50B.
colors: Warm browns of wood and skin tones with a green window and green cash, plus red accents on the arrow, gift and girl's top. The white headline pops on the darker wall, but the red accents compete with the arrow in the right half.
psychology: The seated man has a flat mouth and a straight-ahead look, while the four on the right have open-mouth smiles and lean toward him. The visible contrast of one reserved figure against several smiling ones reads as isolation versus attention.
partnership: The title lists wealth levels from $0 to $50B; the thumbnail shows a single rich-looking state, so it adds the visual reaction but hides the escalation promised by the title. The unanswered question is what changes at poorer levels.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: white headline first, then the red arrow down to the smiling woman, then the cash pile, with the man's face and the gift last.
art: Colourful illustrated style at only 360x202 native, so linework is soft and faces are small compared with other batch images. Lighting is consistent warm interior light and the objects are coherent; no artefacts found, though detail is lost at 160x90.
strength: The cash-versus-crowd picture tells the wealth reaction story without extra words.
weakness: Only one wealth stage is shown, so the title's range from $0 to $50B is not visible.
bottleneck: Low native resolution and five people make faces and the gift a blur at phone size.
action: Hypothesis: split the frame into a poor-state and a rich-state half using the same table and test whether showing the range lifts the title match.
counterexample: Seq 11 uses a clean two-panel split with one figure each, where the comparison is easier to read at 160x90.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: A large cartoon man's head and shoulders fills the left half: spiky black hair with grey-purple tips, narrowed eyes glancing to his right, a closed smile and a pink polo. His pointing index finger extends toward three glossy wordless logos that are dripping: a black interlaced knot with black drips, a blue-to-purple four-point star with blue drips, and an orange starburst with orange drips. Above them S&P 500 is crossed out by a red horizontal bar.
mechanism: Visual replacement: the index being struck out while three melting-style logos sit beneath it implies a switch away from a standard investment, with the pointing hand directing attention to the substitutes.
composition: The man is anchored to the left with a diagonal finger pointing right; the struck-out S&P 500 is the upper-right focal point and the three logos form a horizontal row beneath it. Large white space on the right keeps each of the four items separate.
typography: Two words in heavy black capitals with a red strikethrough, readable in the 160 render; the red bar remains visible. The thumbnail has no words about AI or investing, so the title carries Because of AI and the logos carry the idea visually.
colors: White ground, black headline, and a limited set of strong accent colours on the logos: black, blue-violet and orange. A single red line is the strongest warm accent and marks negation; the pink shirt is a tertiary colour.
psychology: The narrowed eyes pointed sideways, one raised eyebrow and a small smile read as a knowing or confident look in cartoon terms. The pointing finger is a clear direction cue toward the logos.
partnership: Title says changing how I invest because of AI; the thumbnail supplies the S&P 500 that is being dropped and the three logos replacing it, which complements without repeating. The unanswered part is what the replacement actually is.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: struck-out S&P 500 first, then the man's narrowed eyes and finger, then the three dripping logos in left-to-right order.
art: Illustration with glossy 3D-like drip rendering on the logos against a flat cartoon face; the drips on each logo are consistent in direction and lighting. The finger and head are well drawn and the layout keeps three small logos visible at 160x90.
strength: The strikethrough over a familiar index with replacement icons gives a one-glance narrative.
weakness: The logos are wordless, so a viewer who does not recognise the symbols gets no AI cue from the thumbnail alone.
bottleneck: Recognition of the three dripping logos has to be done by the viewer, because no text names them.
action: Hypothesis: add one short word such as AI near the logos and test whether naming the category improves recognition for viewers unfamiliar with the symbols.
counterexample: Seq 14 has no readable cue at all, so the comparison shows how much the struck-out text and logos here carry.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: A cartoon man with an egg-shaped head, one eye squinted in a wink-like narrowing and a toothy grin, stands at left in a white open-collar shirt with rolled sleeves, blue jeans and brown shoes, with an index finger against his chin. At the top right the headline has a grey pixelated block hiding the middle of the number. A thick black curved arrow from PER MONTH sweeps down to an open black briefcase packed with banded green bills.
mechanism: A censored income figure plus a briefcase of cash sets a withheld-number puzzle; the arrow from the monthly figure to the cash links the hidden amount to the money.
composition: The man occupies the left third; the headline fills the upper right in two stacked lines, and the arrow carries the eye diagonally down to the briefcase at lower right. The layout reads as a clear Z shape on a white ground.
typography: Three words in thick black capitals, the first token being a dollar sign, a pixelated square and K. PER MONTH is very large and remains legible at 160x90; the pixelated block is also visible as a grey patch.
colors: White background with black text, the saturated green of the bills as the only strong colour, and skin and brown tones on the man. The green stack is the single colour accent so it stands out.
psychology: The squinted eye, wide grin and finger-at-chin pose read as a coy or secretive look in cartoon terms. The censored block signals withholding, and the briefcase stands for a large amount.
partnership: Title says I'm Nick, Here's How I Make Money; the thumbnail adds a monthly income form with the amount hidden, which is information the title lacks. The hidden value is the main open question.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: pixelated dollar figure first, then PER MONTH, then the arrow to the briefcase of cash, with the grinning man last.
art: Flat vector cartoon with consistent outlines; the briefcase and bills are a small stock-like clip-art cluster. A faint grey vertical edge runs at the far left, and the pixelation is a deliberate block rather than an error.
strength: The hidden amount creates a clean open question with a direct visual answer type.
weakness: Cash-in-a-briefcase imagery is a generic money trope and the figure is intentionally unreadable.
bottleneck: Credibility is limited because the number is obscured and the proof is only a clip-art briefcase.
action: Hypothesis: replace the pixel block with a partly visible real figure and test whether a concrete number increases perceived credibility.
counterexample: Seq 12 puts a fully readable $10,000 figure in the same layout, so it gives a concrete number where this one hides it.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: A stick-figure body with an oversized shaggy-haired bearded head slumps against a cave wall, the face tinted pale green with half-lidded eyes and a slightly open mouth. Around him lie skulls and long bones: a pile of about five skulls with crossed bones at lower left, a cluster of three skulls in the middle, and a full skeleton with ribcage and skull sprawled at lower right. A dark tunnel opening is at right and a 7:33 duration badge sits in the bottom-right corner.
mechanism: A first-person dying quote above a figure seated among skeletons makes the stakes explicit before any context, with the bone piles as proof of earlier failures.
composition: The headline spans the top; the seated figure sits left of centre as the main subject, with skulls framing the bottom edge in a diagonal toward the tunnel. The dark cave opening at right creates depth. The foreground bones are large and crowd the lower third.
typography: Three words in thick yellow capitals with a black outline in single quote marks; they read easily at 160x90 against the dark grey cave. The duration badge is the only other text. The words give the emotion but not the topic of sickness, which the title adds.
colors: Muted grey-brown cave and bone tones with a single bright yellow headline for strong separation. The green tint on the face is the only colour on the figure and signals illness semantically.
psychology: The pale green face, drooping lids and slack open mouth, together with the surrounding skeletons, read as exhaustion and dread in cartoon terms. The quote marks make it a spoken line.
partnership: Title asks what early humans did when they got sick; the thumbnail answers the stakes with a dying figure and skeletons, which escalates the title rather than repeating it. The open question is what they did in response.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: yellow quote first, then the green-faced figure, then the large skulls at lower left, with the dark tunnel last.
art: Hand-drawn style with a stick-figure body under a detailed head and realistic-looking skulls and bones. Shading is consistent across the cave and bones; the head and skeletons use more detail than the body, and no obvious artefacts are visible. At 160x90 the figure and skulls still read.
strength: Yellow quote on a dark scene makes a vivid stake that holds up at phone size.
weakness: The skeleton piles are heavy and the topic of illness is not visible beyond the green face.
bottleneck: The scene shows death but not the illness or a response, so the viewer must rely on the title for the actual question.
action: Hypothesis: add one illness cue such as a visible symptom or a herb beside the figure and test whether the sickness link becomes clearer without the title.
counterexample: Seq 6 uses the same yellow headline style but a bright, active scene, so it frames the topic positively where this one frames it with dread.
hero_object: skulls and bones around seated figure
medical_notes: A historical illness dramatisation with no treatment, cure or diagnostic claim in the visible text.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: A stick-figure character with shaggy brown hair, wide round eyes and a flat mouth line walks across a green slope wearing a ragged fur tunic. He carries a stack of logs behind his neck with a stone axe on top, a wicker basket of grapes and fruit on one arm and a bowl holding a steak and bone in the other hand. Far up the hill on the right a smaller stick figure drags a brown animal hide. The sky is flat blue.
mechanism: A rhetorical question over a heavily loaded caveman answers itself visually: he is hauling logs, food and tools uphill, so the image implies work without any gym.
composition: The heavily loaded figure is centred as the main subject with the diagonal green hillside leading up to the small second figure at right, which gives a secondary read. Blue sky above and green ground below create two flat bands, and the headline sits across the top.
typography: Two words with a question mark in thick yellow capitals with black outline occupy the top fifth and are fully readable in the 160 render. The text does not say ancient or humans, so the caveman costume and the title carry that.
colors: Strong flat sky blue and grass green, a yellow headline that pops against the blue, and brown for the fur and logs. The colours are high-saturation and the figure separates well from the sky.
psychology: The wide round eyes and flat mouth read as a plain, matter-of-fact stare, while the amount carried shows effort. No danger or urgency signals are visible beyond the question mark.
partnership: Title says Why Didn't Ancient Humans Need Exercise; the thumbnail compresses it to NO EXERCISE? and answers with the load-carrying scene, which duplicates much of the title question while adding the answer in pictures. Some curiosity may be resolved before the click.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: yellow question first, then the loaded caveman's face, then the logs and basket, with the tiny figure on the slope last.
art: Flat doodle style with simple outlines and an unrealistic but coherent hillside; the carried items are all clearly separate objects. The second figure is very small at 160x90 but the main figure and headline hold.
strength: Everything the caveman carries shows effort at a glance in a very clean flat scene.
weakness: The question mark invites a yes or no reading and the small figure on the hill adds little.
bottleneck: Hook strength is moderate because the thumbnail nearly answers its own question.
action: Hypothesis: add a modern figure on a treadmill at the corner and test whether a contrast pair gives the question more tension.
mechanism_secondary: rhetorical question answered by visual load
counterexample: Seq 15 uses a similar flat-colour question headline but leaves the answer unseen, so it holds more curiosity than this one.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: A cartoon man with an egg-shaped head and half-lidded eyes looking to his right kneels on one knee at left with a closed-mouth smile, wearing a white shirt and blue jeans. In his raised left hand is a calculator with a green glow and screen text +1000, and his right fist is clenched near his chest. In the bottom centre a dark wallet with a card poking out sits inside a red glow, with a black arrow from the word DEBT curving down to it. The ground line and background are white.
mechanism: A single concrete number framed by an action verb and a glowing red wallet versus a green-glow calculator, setting up an overcome-the-debt story with colour-coded money objects.
composition: The headline stack takes the upper right, the man the left half, and the wallet the bottom centre; the arrow loops from the number block back to the wallet, making a clockwise path. The black ground line anchors the wallet and the kneeling man.
typography: Three lines in heavy condensed black capitals: CRUSH in medium size, $10,000 very large, DEBT medium. The amount dominates and is legible at 160x90. The text repeats the number and topic of the title and adds the verb crush.
colors: Black on white with two semantic glows: green behind the calculator and red behind the wallet. The man's white shirt and mid-blue jeans stay neutral so the glows pop as the only accents.
psychology: The half-lidded sideways glance and tight smile read as calm or confident in cartoon terms, and the clenched fist suggests determination. The red glow reads as a debt-danger zone on the wallet.
partnership: Title gives Fast Way to Pay Off $10K in Debt on a Small Salary — Step by Step; the thumbnail shares the same $10,000 and debt and adds the crush verb and the green-versus-red cue, which complements it. Details such as small salary and the steps are not shown.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the large $10,000 first, then the wallet in the red glow via the arrow, then the man's face, with the glowing calculator last.
art: Flat vector cartoon with consistent outlines; the green and red glows are applied as soft halos and look slightly pasted on. The wallet and calculator are readable at 160x90 but the +1000 screen text is not.
strength: One huge number with a green-versus-red object pair makes the money story readable in a glance.
weakness: The calculator screen text and wallet card are too small to read at phone size, and the man's pose does not clearly show crushing.
bottleneck: The crush verb has no visual action, since the debt is only a wallet in a red glow.
action: Hypothesis: show the red wallet being squashed or cracked and test whether a visible crushing action improves the match with the verb.
counterexample: Seq 4 hides its number behind a pixel block while this one prints $10,000 in full, so Seq 4 gives less concrete proof at the same layout.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

text: 1 COMMON PILL / DAMAGES / YOUR BRAIN / AFTER 60 / DON'T TAKE IT [Dr. Okoro, MD name tag]
scene: On the right a man with a grey beard and furrowed brows in teal scrubs and a teal surgical cap rests one hand on his cap and raises an index finger toward the camera; a stethoscope hangs on his neck and a name tag reads Dr. Okoro, MD. A white inset box at lower left shows an orange pill bottle labelled OTC crossed out by a red X, white tablets, a red lightning bolt and a brain cross-section with visible folds. A red curved arrow from AFTER 60 points down to the inset. The left panel is dark navy and the right panel is red.
mechanism: A prescriber-style authority figure issues a warning against a pill, while the inset connects the crossed-out bottle to a damaged-looking brain image to make the claimed harm visible.
composition: A split frame with a text column on the left and the pointing figure filling the right third, so the face and raised finger sit at the edge. The red arrow and inset form a diagonal from the headline down toward the bottom centre. Five lines of text plus the inset leave little negative space.
typography: Five lines of mixed yellow and white capitals with purple highlight boxes behind DAMAGES and AFTER 60 give high density. The first three lines survive at 160x90, but the inset labels and the name tag are unreadable. The thumbnail adds brain damage and age 60, which the title does not state.
colors: A dark navy text panel and a saturated red panel with teal scrubs, yellow and purple highlights and white text. Red is used for the right background, arrow and X, signalling alarm; the combination is loud and has many competing accents.
psychology: The furrowed brows, tight mouth, hand on the head and raised finger read as a stern warning posture. Medical dress, a stethoscope and the name tag are authority cues, while the damaged brain adds a fear cue.
partnership: Title says The 1 Common Pill I'd Never Let My Parents Take Daily; the thumbnail escalates with a specific harm (damages your brain) and an age (after 60) while still not naming the pill. The unnamed pill is the open question.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: yellow 1 COMMON PILL first, then the stern face and raised finger on the right, then the highlighted DAMAGES and the arrow to the brain inset.
art: Photographic cutout of the figure on a red field alongside rendered pill and brain graphics; the lighting on the person is flat and the inset is a clean icon-like composite. The cutout edges are tidy, and the inset is too small to read at 160x90.
strength: The strong authority figure plus a harm headline creates a clear warning proposition.
weakness: Five text lines, three colours, a name tag and an inset make a crowded design with unreadable small elements.
bottleneck: The unqualified claim that a pill damages the brain after 60 has no visible source, so credibility is weak.
action: Hypothesis: cut the text to two lines (PILL + BRAIN HARM) and test whether a cleaner layout with a less absolute claim keeps the warning legible.
counterexample: Seq 13 has no text or alarm cue, so it is the opposite of this crowded warning design.
medical_notes: The packaging asserts brain damage from an unnamed common pill after age 60 with a crossed-out bottle and brain image but no named drug or visible source.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: An extreme close-up of the lower half of an older person's wrinkled face fills the right half: nose, open mouth and extended pink tongue with two dark dried cloves lying on it, a gold earring and a beige knit collar at the edges. At lower left two stacked before-and-after pairs are joined by red arrows: a colon with dark brown clumps in a red glow becomes a clean pink colon in a golden glow, and a lumpy yellow-orange liver becomes a smooth dark red liver in a golden glow. The background behind the text is a red-to-orange gradient.
mechanism: A tiny daily action (one clove) is paired with organ before-and-after graphics and a SHOCK headline to imply a rapid internal transformation within a week.
composition: The giant face crop dominates the right with the tongue and cloves as focal point at lower right; the headline occupies the top-left and the two insets stack below it, making a left text-and-diagram column opposite the face. The red arrows point right, from each before panel to its after panel. Little negative space remains.
typography: Two lines of heavy capitals, white for 1 CLOVE A DAY and yellow for 7-DAY SHOCK, with six words in total across the top left, readable at 160x90. The inset organs read as colour blocks only. The thumbnail drops the word IRREVERSIBLE that the title uses and adds the organs as the unstated target.
colors: Hot red-orange gradient with yellow and white text, pink skin and tongue, and gold glows on the after panels. Brown-clumped colon and bumpy yellow liver versus clean pink and dark red organs encode bad versus good through colour.
psychology: The face is cropped above the eyes, so no expression is shown; the extended tongue with cloves is a direct, slightly unsettling close-up. The SHOCK headline, glow and red arrows carry the urgency cues; the wrinkled skin stands for older age visually.
partnership: Title says Chew 1 Clove Every Morning. After 7 Days Your Body Goes Through IRREVERSIBLE Changes; the thumbnail repeats the clove and seven days and shows the organs affected, which fills in what changes while the title sells permanence. The open question is how a single clove could produce such organ results.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: white and yellow headline first, then the cloves on the tongue at right, then the red-glow colon-and-liver before and after panels.
art: High-gloss rendering with exaggerated glowing organs next to a photographic mouth close-up; the organ images are stylised graphics and their golden halos differ in lighting from the photo, so the elements read as composited. The clumped colon and lumpy liver are not realistic medical images, and the insets are crude at 160x90.
strength: Bold two-line headline and a striking close-up with cloves create an instant and unusual visual hook.
weakness: Dramatic organ transformation graphics and the SHOCK wording present an extreme body result with no visible source.
bottleneck: Credibility is the limiting factor because the organ before-and-afters stand in for a medical outcome from a single spice.
action: Hypothesis: replace the organ before-and-after insets with one modest labelled benefit claim and test whether a restrained version keeps interest with less implied reversal.
counterexample: Seq 13 contains no claim imagery at all, so Seq 13 is the low-claim opposite of these glowing organ transformations.
medical_notes: Colon and liver before-and-after graphics tied to one clove a day imply organ repair, and the title adds IRREVERSIBLE, without any visible evidence.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: A cartoon man with an egg-shaped head, wide round eyes looking right and an open mouth stands at left in a grey T-shirt and blue jeans with both hands clasped at his chest. At the lower right a single banded bundle of bills labelled 50% sits beside a red curved arrow that sweeps up to a large heap of banded stacks of bills. Black DOUBLE sits above a yellow highlight box holding YOUR FUTURE.
mechanism: A small labelled stack becomes a much larger heap through an arrow, which turns the title's half-income idea into a growth picture with a headline verb.
composition: The man fills the left third, the headline stack the upper right and the money diagram the lower right, so the layout reads as three clear zones. The red arrow rises left to right and ends on the largest object, the heap, the secondary focal point after the headline.
typography: Three text elements: DOUBLE in large black capitals, YOUR FUTURE inside a yellow bar, and a small 50% above the single stack. The headline and the yellow bar are readable at 160x90 but the 50% label is tiny. The thumbnail introduces the half-income number that the title spells out as half.
colors: White ground with black type, a yellow highlight bar, green cash and a red arrow. The red arrow is the only warm accent against the greens, and the grey shirt is neutral.
psychology: The wide eyes, open mouth and clasped hands read as eager or excited in cartoon terms. Money piles of different sizes carry the growth cue; no danger signals are shown.
partnership: Title says What Happens When You Invest Half Your Income; the thumbnail adds the double outcome and the 50% figure, which complements the question while giving away the answer as a big pile. The open question is how the doubling is reached.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: black DOUBLE first, then the yellow YOUR FUTURE bar, then the red arrow up to the large cash pile, with the excited man and 50% last.
art: Flat cartoon vector with consistent outlines and clean stacks of bills; the heap is built from repeated identical bundles. The layout is simple and holds up at phone size, although the 50% label is small.
strength: A small-to-large cash picture with a growth arrow explains the idea without reading.
weakness: The 50% label is too small to read at phone size, and the doubling is a generic claim without a timeframe.
bottleneck: The key number 50% is the smallest text on the frame, so the main condition for the promise is buried.
action: Hypothesis: enlarge 50% to a badge on the small stack and test whether the cause-and-effect pair reads at 160x90.
mechanism_secondary: growth diagram with small input stack
counterexample: Seq 7 puts its number at maximum size, so the key figure survives phone size where this one does not.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: A black vertical line splits the frame in two panels on white. The left panel has 90% in huge black numerals above a smiling stick figure with wide round eyes holding a blue pencil that has written RIGHT in blue. The right panel has 10% above a stick figure with sweat drops on its head, furrowed brows and gritted teeth holding a red pencil beside the word LEFT in rough red lettering with motion scribbles around it and around its arm.
mechanism: A proportion comparison rendered as two matched stick-figure panels, where the calm blue handwriting and the strained red handwriting turn the 90 versus 10 split into a visible contrast.
composition: A strict mirror split along a central line, with each panel stacking number, figure and word in the same order. The huge percentages take the upper half and the figures the lower half. White space is generous and symmetrical, so the only difference between sides is the figure's state and colour.
typography: Four words, two giant black percent figures and a small blue and red word each, all readable at 160x90; the percentages dominate. The thumbnail adds the 90 percent right-handed counterpart that the title only implies with Exactly 10% Left-Handed.
colors: Black numerals on white with one blue and one red accent assigned to the two halves. Blue pencil and word versus red pencil and word give a calm-versus-strained colour code and the high contrast keeps each half distinct.
psychology: The left figure has a smile and relaxed pose, while the right figure has sweat drops, furrowed brows, gritted teeth and trembling lines. Those visible cues show ease versus strain without any real person involved.
partnership: Title asks Why Are Exactly 10% of People Left-Handed; the thumbnail answers the proportion with 90 and 10 and sets a posed contrast, which complements without giving the cause. The open question is why left-handers are the minority.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: huge 90% first, then 10% opposite it, then the sweating right-hand figure, with the pencil words RIGHT and LEFT read last.
art: Clean hand-drawn stick figures with consistent line weight; pencil, sweat drops and scribble marks are simple and all object parts are coherent. The composition remains crisp at 160x90, with no clutter.
strength: A mirrored 90 versus 10 split gives a clear comparison that survives at tiny size.
weakness: The two figures differ only in expression and pencil colour, so the specific topic of handedness is carried by a small word under each number.
bottleneck: The hand on which each figure writes is shown only by the small RIGHT and LEFT words, which are the least dominant elements.
action: Hypothesis: draw the 10 percent figure holding the pencil in its left hand and the other in the right so handedness shows without reading the small words.
counterexample: Seq 2 has a similar contrast but crowds five faces into one room, while this one keeps each side to one figure.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: A cartoon man with an egg-shaped head, eyes glancing down to his right and a closed-mouth neutral look stands at left in a dark grey-blue button shirt with rolled sleeves, holding a single green banknote with a portrait and a large 1 and 0 at its ends. A thick black curved arrow from the word FORMULA points down to a block of banded bill stacks arranged in three columns at lower centre. The background is white.
mechanism: A named formula attached to a large dollar figure and a block of cash makes a specific, concrete payoff promise, while the single bill in the man's hands and the stacks create a small-to-large pair.
composition: The man takes the left half, the stacked headline occupies the upper right, and the arrow runs down-left to the cash stacks, which place the secondary focus at lower centre. The layout is a near copy of a left-character and right-headline grid with a lot of white space.
typography: Three lines of heavy condensed black capitals with $10,000 largest, readable at 160x90 where only the figure and FORMULA stay strong. The thumbnail repeats the title's $10K and formula and adds no information about savings or normal incomes.
colors: White background with black text, green bills as the lone saturated colour and a muted blue-grey shirt. Colour has no semantic highlighting apart from green for money, so the frame feels monochrome apart from the cash.
psychology: The side-glancing eyes and closed mouth read as composed or reserved in cartoon terms, with no strong emotion visible. The money in his hand and the stacks are the only cues.
partnership: Title says The $10K Savings Formula (That Works on Normal Incomes); the thumbnail repeats $10,000 and formula without savings or normal-income qualifiers, so the visual supplies only generic cash. The open question is what the formula is.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: big $10,000 first, then FORMULA and the arrow, then the cash stacks, with the man's face and the single bill last.
art: Flat vector cartoon matching a consistent outline weight; the bill in his hand shows a portrait with a 1 at its left end and a 0 at its right end, which does not match the $10,000 figure. The simple layout is clean but the same figure type is reused with little variation.
strength: A single big figure plus FORMULA frames a crisp, concrete promise at a glance.
weakness: The expression is neutral and the scene looks like a template, so little tension supports the number.
bottleneck: Nothing in the image says savings or normal incomes, so the title's qualifier is missing from the visual.
action: Hypothesis: replace the neutral pose with a visible small paycheck beside the stacks and test whether it conveys the normal-incomes angle.
counterexample: Seq 11 uses a split comparison with strong contrasting expressions, while this thumbnail keeps one neutral figure and so shows less tension.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

mechanism: A stock-style yoga-pose frame with no overlay text; it relies solely on the posed figure to signal an exercise topic.
composition: The figure is placed centrally in a narrow column with a symmetrical outstretched-arm pose, and the two blank blurred side bars take about two thirds of the frame width. The head is well below the top, with windows behind for strong backlight. There is no secondary focal point beyond the mat.
typography: No text appears. Everything the title says, including reverse aging and cells, is absent from the image, so the thumbnail adds nothing in words.
colors: Soft neutral palette of cream, beige and black clothing with a teal mat as the only saturated accent, while the pillar bars are flat grey-green. The black outfit separates from the beige wall, but overall contrast is low.
psychology: The woman shows a neutral, forward-directed face and a balanced posture with arms spread. No urgency, fear or hope cues are visible, so the emotion is calm.
partnership: Title promises reverse aging through exercise; the thumbnail shows a person exercising, which is related but gives no visible aging, cell or reversal cue. The thumbnail carries almost no extra promise, leaving the whole hook to the title.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: bright window area and the black outfit in the centre first, then the arms spread wide, then the teal mat below, with the blurred side bars ignored.
art: Realistic photo frame with natural window light and consistent shadows on the mat; no compositing artefacts visible. The pillarbox wastes most of the 16:9 area, so at 160x90 the person is small and her face cannot be read.
strength: A clean, well-lit exercise pose communicates the topic with no clutter.
weakness: Two thirds of the frame is blank blurred bars, and no text or cue says aging, cells or results.
bottleneck: The vertical-video pillarbox shrinks the only subject to a narrow strip at phone size.
action: Hypothesis: crop the vertical frame to fill 16:9 around the pose and add two or three words naming the aging claim to test whether subject size and a text cue raise relevance.
counterexample: Seq 11 fills the full frame with two clear panels and large numerals, so it is the opposite of this narrow, wordless frame.

colors: Muted brown and tan with black and white eyes and a pure white background band; the saturation is low and all colour is in one warm family. The white eyes are the highest-contrast elements.
psychology: Wide round eyes with eye-bag hatching and a flat straight mouth form a blank, stunned-looking cartoon stare. No money, warning or hope cue accompanies it.
partnership: Title says Inflation #animation #finance; the thumbnail shows an expressionless face with no price, money or chart cue, so the title carries the whole topic. The image offers curiosity about the face but nothing about inflation.

art: Simple hand-drawn cartoon with flat tan fill and thick line; the crop is arbitrary and the white bands look like a vertical frame placed on a 16:9 canvas. The face stays readable at 160x90, but most of the canvas is empty.

weakness: The frame carries no finance or inflation cue, and white and brown bars take most of the canvas.

scene: A stick-figure hiker with a round white head, wide eyes glancing to his right and a small uneasy closed mouth stands on the left in a blue jacket, brown trousers and a brown backpack with a rolled bedroll. A winding brown path leads through a blue-grey pine forest with a few brown trees. At the right a grey wolf walks toward the right edge with its head turned back over its shoulder at the hiker, showing wide eyes and raised brows.
mechanism: A first-contact encounter between a hiker and a wolf who both look wary turns the question into a visible reversal: the wolf looks nervous too.
composition: The hiker on the left and the wolf on the right balance each other at about the same height, with the winding path leading from the lower left into the scene. The yellow headline fills the top and the grey-blue forest is low contrast behind the figures. The two eye-lines meet in the middle.
typography: Three words in thick yellow capitals with black outline and a question mark fill the top width, readable at 160x90 against the blue-grey sky and trees. The question uses US, putting the viewer in the position of the hiker, and the title adds the word Attack.
colors: Cool blue-grey forest with brown path and tree accents, a blue jacket for the hiker and a yellow headline as the highest-contrast element. The wolf is grey on grey-blue, so it separates less strongly than the hiker.
psychology: The hiker's raised glance and tight mouth, and the wolf's wide eyes, raised brows and back-turned head, read as mutual wariness in cartoon terms. There is no aggression cue such as bared teeth.
partnership: Title says Why Don't Wild Wolves Attack Us; the thumbnail swaps attack for avoid and shows a wolf that seems wary, which complements the question but shifts the framing from danger to avoidance. The open question is why the wolf keeps away.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: yellow headline first, then the hiker's face, then the wolf's worried eyes at right, with the winding path last.
art: Flat stick-figure hiker beside a more detailed shaded wolf; the mix of styles is consistent in line weight, and the forest uses simple repeating tree shapes. The wolf is slightly low contrast against the forest but still readable at 160x90.
strength: Two wary faces facing each other create an instant story from the question.
weakness: The wolf blends into the blue-grey forest, so its face is less visible than the hiker's.
bottleneck: The cool low-contrast scene gives the wolf, the second protagonist, less emphasis than the headline and hiker.
action: Hypothesis: lighten the wolf or place a pale rim behind it and test whether a clearer second protagonist improves the reading at 160x90.
counterexample: Seq 6 uses a bold blue-green yellow-headline scene of the same style where the loaded figure is the single focus, so there is no second protagonist to compete with it.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: A red banner across the top carries white capitals. On a dark navy background with a blue glow a bare older foot and ankle fill the left half, showing purple-blue branching vein lines and a glowing red patch at the ankle marked by a red arrow. At right a man with swept-back grey hair and a grey moustache in navy scrubs with a stethoscope points a finger toward the foot with a closed-mouth slight smile. At bottom left a circular inset shows a person's legs in black leggings rising onto toes beside a wooden chair, with a yellow upward arrow.
mechanism: A symptom question in a red banner plus a vein-covered, glowing red ankle sets a problem, while the pointing doctor and the exercise inset promise a quick fix to do.
composition: The red banner spans the top, the foot runs diagonally from top-left to the centre, DO THIS in yellow is at the centre, the doctor fills the right third and the exercise inset anchors the bottom left. The eyes follow the foot to the point of the doctor's finger. The elements are layered but separated by the dark background.
typography: Five words in two lines: white capitals on a red bar and yellow DO THIS in the centre, readable at 160x90. The inset content, the toe-raise legs and the small arrows are unreadable at that size. The text asks the condition question and adds a command, while the title adds one exercise and the age 70.
colors: Dark navy background with blue glow, a red banner and red glowing ankle patch, yellow DO THIS and navy scrubs. Red works as a problem and alarm signal in the banner and the glowing ankle, and yellow marks the instruction.
psychology: The doctor has a calm, slight smile, direct gaze and pointing finger that read as reassuring authority, in contrast to the glowing red ankle and purple veins, which carry the alarm. The stethoscope and scrubs are authority cues.
partnership: Title says SURGEON REVEALS: Do This 1 Exercise for Poor Leg Circulation After 70; the thumbnail repeats the poor circulation question and do this and shows an exercise inset, but leaves out the age and the single-exercise count. The unanswered question is what the exercise is.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: red banner first, then the glowing red ankle and arrow, then yellow DO THIS, then the doctor's pointing hand and face.
art: Photographic-style render with dramatic rim lighting; the ankle skin texture shows exaggerated vein patterns and a glowing red region that looks digitally enhanced. The doctor appears as a separate cutout with a flat blue edge light, and the inset is a small composite that is not readable at 160x90.
strength: Symptom banner, foot close-up and pointing doctor assemble a problem-to-solution story quickly.
weakness: The exaggerated glowing veins and the unreadable exercise inset leave the actual solution unseen at phone size.
bottleneck: The solution is only a small circular inset, so the DO THIS command points to something the viewer cannot read.
action: Hypothesis: enlarge the toe-raise inset to a third of the frame and drop one other element to test whether the visible exercise makes DO THIS concrete.
counterexample: Seq 8 uses the same authority-plus-alarm approach with a pill and brain, but makes the harm claim rather than a fix.
medical_notes: The glowing vein-covered ankle exaggerates a circulation symptom and the surgeon claim has no visible name or credential beyond scrubs.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

text: STOOL STUCK / IN THE RECTUM / NO STRENGTH / TO PUSH! / LEARN WHAT TO DO
scene: At the right an older cartoon man with thin grey hair, a lined forehead and a downturned mouth sits on a white toilet pressing both hands against the sides of his head. He wears a light-blue short-sleeve shirt that ends at the thighs, bare legs and brown slippers. The background is solid black, and the last line of text sits in a red rectangle at the bottom left.
mechanism: A blunt symptom statement stacked in four lines next to a hunched figure on a toilet turns an embarrassing problem into a recognisable scene, then promises a remedy with a bottom call-to-action bar.
composition: Text stacks on the left two thirds in descending lines, and the seated man fills the right third and the full height of the frame. His bowed head with hands on the temples, plus the white toilet, forms one compact shape against black. A red bar anchors the bottom left, so the eye runs top-left to bottom-left to the figure.
typography: Thirteen words across five lines: the first two in huge yellow capitals, then white capitals, then white-on-red LEARN WHAT TO DO. All lines stay readable at 160x90, and the large size makes the symptom plain. The words restate the title's problem and add the no-strength detail and a command, but not the medical term for the condition.
colors: Black background with large yellow and white capitals and a red label bar, plus the light-blue shirt and tan skin of the figure. Yellow on black and the red bar read as an alarm-style palette that has high contrast.
psychology: The man has a furrowed forehead, drooping mouth and both hands pressed to his head, a visible distress pose in cartoon terms. The aged features, hair and slippers are visible age cues. The embarrassing setting adds a vulnerability cue.
partnership: Title says Stool STUCK in the Rectum! What is it and what to do?; the thumbnail repeats the stuck wording and adds no strength to push and a learn-what-to-do command, which complements it. The open question is the cause and remedy.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: huge yellow STOOL STUCK first, then the distressed man at right, then the white NO STRENGTH TO PUSH line, with the red bar read last.
art: Flat vector illustration with simple shading and consistent outlines; the man's anatomy and the toilet are coherent. The layout has no clutter and holds up at 160x90, although the character's face is small relative to the text.
strength: Large high-contrast text and a clear distressed figure make the topic unmistakable even at 160x90.
weakness: Five lines of text leave little room for the image and the crude toilet pose may be off-putting.
bottleneck: The text dominates the frame, so the picture adds only a distress pose and no clue about the answer.
action: Hypothesis: shorten to two lines and add one small visual cue of the remedy, for example a glass of water, to test whether a hint of the fix improves the promise.
counterexample: Seq 16 includes a small exercise inset that visualises the fix, where this thumbnail only shows the problem.
medical_notes: Names a rectal symptom with dramatic wording and a learn-what-to-do promise but shows no treatment claim, so the video must supply the safe guidance.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: A vertical frame is pillarboxed with blurred brown bars on both sides, and the centre column shows a bearded man with glasses and dark hair in a dark navy T-shirt, both palms turned up in a questioning shrug and mouth slightly open. In front of him on a wooden board sits a large white bowl of oatmeal with steam, a bag labelled INSTANT OATS stands behind it at left, and a glowing red zig-zag line with dots climbs steeply from the bowl to above his head. A small tablet showing a lower red line graph is visible behind the bowl.
mechanism: A two-word question pair, with HEALTHY in white and SPIKE in red, sits over a bowl of oats and a red glucose-style spike line, framing a trusted-food-versus-danger question with a gesturing presenter.
composition: Two stacked words occupy the upper left of the centre column, the presenter on the right and the bowl lower left, with the red spike line connecting bowl to words. The arrangement is clustered into a narrow column that fills only about a third of the frame width, with blurred bars on both sides.
typography: Two words with question marks stacked at top, white HEALTHY and red SPIKE, readable at 160x90 although the column is narrow. INSTANT OATS on the bag is tiny at phone size. The thumbnail does not say blood sugar, diabetes or seniors, which the title adds.
colors: Warm brown blurred bars and dark background, a glowing red spike line and red SPIKE as the single hot accent, with cream oats and a white bowl as the light object. The red-versus-white pair encodes alarm versus health in the text.
psychology: The man has raised brows, an open mouth and both palms up in a questioning gesture, which reads as asking the viewer a question. The steep red line and red word give a clear alarm cue.
partnership: Title says Instant Oatmeal and Blood Sugar: What Seniors With Diabetes Should Know; the thumbnail adds a graph spike and healthy-versus-spike question, so it complements the title by showing the concern. The answer to the question is left open.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: white HEALTHY then red SPIKE first, then the glowing red line down to the oatmeal bowl, then the presenter's open palms and face.
art: Photographic presenter with a realistic bowl and an overlaid glowing line graph; the overlay is clean and its dots are crisp. The vertical-video pillarbox means the picture uses a fraction of the 16:9 frame, so at 160x90 the person and bowl are small.
strength: Two short words and a red spike line explain the doubt over oatmeal in a single glance.
weakness: The pillarbox reduces the picture to a narrow centre column and the INSTANT OATS bag text is too small to read.
bottleneck: The wasted side bars shrink everything, so the product and graph shrink below comfortable phone size.
action: Hypothesis: crop the vertical frame to a 16:9 version centred on the bowl and the spike line and test whether the larger scale of the key objects improves readability.
counterexample: Seq 14 uses the same pillarboxed layout but has no text or topic object, so Seq 14 shows what this frame would lose without its question words.
hero_object: oatmeal bowl with red spike line
medical_notes: The image asks whether instant oats spike blood sugar with a red spike graphic but gives no verdict, so the answer depends on the video content.

text: ROCKEFELLER / ROTHSCHILD / VANDERBILT / CARNEGIE / WINDSOR / MELLON / FORD / BOURBON / KENNEDY / HABSBURG / MEDICI / ASTOR
scene: Twelve black-outlined colour circles in a grid of four columns and three rows, each holding a black line-art emblem with a family name beneath. Row three: a shamrock on cyan, a double-headed eagle on yellow, a stack of coins on lavender, a beaver on red. The background is white.
mechanism: A catalogue grid of twelve named family crests promises a complete roster, with each emblem standing in for a dynasty.
composition: A rigid four-by-three grid with equal circle sizes leaves no single focal point; the eye drifts across the saturated circles. The bottom row of names sits right at the lower edge of the frame, so its letters are tightly cropped.
typography: Twelve single-word names in thick black rounded capitals and lower case mix, each under its circle; they are readable at 320x180 but they shrink to unreadable dots at 160x90 while the colours still show. The thumbnail has no headline and does not mention old money or ten minutes, which the title supplies.
colors: A high-saturation rainbow of green, red, blue, yellow, magenta, orange, mint, cyan and lavender fills, each against bold black outlines. The colours do not carry meaning, and the palette is loud with no accent among the twelve.
psychology: There are no faces or people, only animal and object emblems, so no emotion is shown. The names of famous families act as recognition cues for viewers who know them.
partnership: Title says Every Old Money Family Dynasty Explained in 10 Minutes; the thumbnail turns the word every into a visible list of twelve names, which supports the completeness promise but does not give any reason to care. The question is which families are on the list.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: bright green and red circles at top left first, then a sweep across the top row and down the grid, with the name labels read last if at all.
art: Clean vector circles with line-art emblems of mixed styles: the dog, eagle and lion are detailed engraving-type drawings while the SUV is an outline sketch, so the set looks stitched together. The grid is orderly but the bottom labels are cropped at the edge.
strength: The grid communicates a full list in one glance, and the bold colours make each circle pop.
weakness: The names are unreadable at phone size and the twelve circles compete equally with no hierarchy.
bottleneck: With no focal element or headline, nothing tells the viewer why the dynasties matter.
action: Hypothesis: enlarge the four most recognisable crests and shrink the rest, then add a short headline such as OLD MONEY and test whether a clear hierarchy improves readability.
counterexample: Seq 11 has two giant figures and a single comparison, so it shows the focal clarity this grid lacks.

mechanism: A salon scene surrounded by six business-metric callouts frames the topic as a business analysis checklist rather than a lifestyle picture.
composition: The headline occupies the top third, the salon is a centred symmetrical storefront and the six ovals sit in two columns at its sides, with arrows converging on the shop. The balanced layout is orderly but the shop interior, ovals and arrows divide attention evenly.
typography: Five words of the headline in huge black capitals and a red underline are readable at 160x90. The six oval labels are small handwritten text and are not readable at phone size, and the BEAUTY SALON sign repeats the headline. The labels add business terms that the title does not state.
colors: White ground with black headline, a black-and-gold salon with warm lights and pink flowers and thin red outlines on the ovals. The gold-and-black interior is the strongest colour block and the red lines only mark the labels.
psychology: No people or faces are visible apart from a stylised portrait and the sign profile, so there is no expression cue. The upscale lighting and the business labels convey a polished, professional tone.
partnership: Title says The Economics of Onwing a Beauty Saloon; the thumbnail reframes it as SO YOU WANT TO OWN A BEAUTY SALON and lists six economic factors, which complements by showing what economics means. The question is how profitable it really is.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the big black headline first, then the gold BEAUTY SALON sign, then the lit mirrors and chairs, with the small ovals on either side read last.

weakness: Six small oval labels are unreadable at phone size and the same format appears to be reused for other businesses.
bottleneck: The informational labels carry the business proposition but are the smallest text on the frame.

counterexample: Seq 7 has one huge number and one object per side, so it shows how a single figure can carry a money topic more simply than six labels.

psychology: The big man shows heavy-lidded eyes and a slight smirk, while the four men behind have narrowed, flat or arms-crossed postures. These are drawn expressions only; no spoken or written claim accompanies them.
partnership: Title says Your Life Driving the Same Car for 10 Years; the thumbnail adds a rusty old car beside newer ones and a staring group, which hints at status contrast but not at the 10-year duration. The unanswered question is how the owner's life turns out.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the big man's face first, then the rusty hood he leans on, then the black sedan with its grille, then the row of four men at right.

weakness: No text and a low-saturation palette make it blend into a grey frame with little pop.

text: SO YOU WANT TO / START A BANK / Interest Income / Non-Interest Income / Loans & Lending / Operating Costs / Regulation & Compliance / Profit & Value / [BANK]

mechanism: A grand bank facade ringed by six revenue and cost labels frames a bank startup as an institutional business model, with the headline giving the challenge in the first person.

colors: Pale cream background with grey stone, gold doors and coins, green bills and a red underline. The palette is soft and mostly neutral, so the gold doors and the green money stacks are the accents.
psychology: No people appear, so there is no expression cue; the classical columns, gold doors and money stacks give a stable, authoritative impression. Nothing signals urgency or fear.
partnership: Title says The Economics of Owning a Bank; the thumbnail reframes it as SO YOU WANT TO START A BANK and lists six cost and revenue concepts, which complements the economics promise by changing the topic from owning to starting. The question is what the economics are.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: big black headline first, then the columned bank facade with the gold doors, then the green cash and coins at the base, with the six labels read last.

A small circular lost LEGACY logo sits in the top-left corner on a white background.

strength: The calm man amid several alarmed faces gives a clear tension that holds up at thumbnail size.
weakness: The scene has no readable text and the savings or $100k link in the title is not visible anywhere.
bottleneck: The crowded garage scene tells a repair-bill story that the viewer cannot connect to the saving promise in the title.
action: Hypothesis: replace the phone figure with a larger readable $100K savings balance in the man's hand and test whether it ties the scene to the title.
